findings.subject: sidebar
findings.summary: A collapsed offcanvas sidebar is moved off-screen but stays focusable and in the accessibility tree, so Tab lands on invisible links.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/sidebar/sidebar.css:149-177 (left/right: calc(var(--sidebar-width) * -1)); grep inert|visibility over sidebar.css and sidebar.tsx returns nothing.
findings.fix: When data-state='collapsed' and collapsible='offcanvas', set inert on the container (or visibility:hidden after the transition) and add a test that collapsed links are not tabbable.

verified.reason: sidebar.tsx:285-305 renders the desktop container with no inert, aria-hidden or visibility toggle when state is collapsed. sidebar.css:169-177 only moves it off-screen with left/right: calc(var(--sidebar-width) * -1), and the container stays display:flex at 768px and wider. grep finds no inert in sidebar.tsx or sidebar.css (the one inert hit is a stories comment). So collapsed offcanvas links stay in the tab order and the accessibility tree. Only the mobile Sheet path handles this.

findings.subject: sidebar-nav-tree
findings.summary: The active nav item is shown by colour only: isActive sets data-active but never aria-current, so screen readers cannot tell which page is current.
findings.evidence: grep -n aria-current over packages/ui-react/src/components/sidebar/sidebar.tsx and packages/ui-react/src/components/sidebar-nav-tree/sidebar-nav-tree.tsx returns nothing; SidebarMenuButton sets 'data-active': isActive (sidebar.tsx:566) and SidebarMenuSubButton likewise (:753); CLI guidance says to expose the current route.
findings.fix: Set aria-current='page' when isActive on SidebarMenuButton/SubButton (link elements), and assert it in sidebar and sidebar-nav-tree tests.

verified.reason: SidebarMenuButton (sidebar.tsx:564) and SidebarMenuSubButton (:752) set only data-active. SidebarNavLinkItem renders the <a href> itself and receives isActive (sidebar-nav-tree.tsx:163-210), yet sets no aria-current. In ui-react, aria-current appears only in pagination, carousel and app-view stories, never in sidebar or sidebar-nav-tree. A tree that owns both the link and the active flag should set the current page itself.

findings.subject: marquee
findings.summary: Marquee loops forever by default with no way for keyboard or touch users to pause it (WCAG 2.2.2, Level A).
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/marquee/marquee.tsx:27 pauseOnHover=false; marquee.test.tsx:89 confirms no tab stop while animating; pause exists only as a developer prop (paused).
findings.fix: Default pauseOnHover to true, pause on focus-within, and ship a pause/play control (or document and enforce one in stories) for strips that run longer than 5s.

verified.reason: The default is real: pauseOnHover=false, so focus-within does not pause either, and there is no built-in control. But prefers-reduced-motion is handled in two places. marquee.css stops the animation and turns the strip into a scroll area, and marquee.tsx makes it a focusable, named group. paused and pauseOnHover are also available. The default only partly meets WCAG 2.2.2, and the motion-sensitive case is covered, so this does not block 'ready'.

findings.subject: marquee
findings.summary: In right-to-left layouts the marquee loop likely leaves a visible empty gap each cycle, because the keyframes always move left while duplicate tracks lay out to the left.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/marquee/marquee.css:51-57 translateX(calc(-100% - var(--gap))); no :dir(rtl) rule (grep). Reasoned from CSS; not rendered.
findings.fix: Add :dir(rtl) keyframes that move right (translateX(calc(100% + var(--gap)))) or force direction:ltr on the track, plus an RTL story and baseline.

verified.reason: Reproduced from the CSS. .a63-Marquee is a flex row with no direction override, so in RTL track 1 starts at the inline-start (right) edge and the duplicate tracks overflow to the left. The keyframe always moves left (translateX(calc(-100% - var(--gap)))), so every cycle opens a blank area one track wide at the right edge before the loop snaps back. There is no :dir(rtl) or dir handling in marquee.tsx or marquee.css. The default loop looks broken on RTL pages. Sidebar already accepts a dir prop, so RTL is in scope.

findings.subject: text-ticker
findings.summary: In right-to-left layouts the text-ticker reveal likely scrolls into blank space and fades the wrong edge; it labels every Sidebar Nav Tree item.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/text-ticker/text-ticker.css:31 'to right' mask, :109-114 translateX(-50%); no RTL rule; sidebar-nav-tree.tsx wraps every string label in TextTicker variant='marquee'. Reasoned from CSS; not rendered.
findings.fix: Mirror the keyframes and mask under :dir(rtl) (or isolate the track with direction:ltr while keeping text direction), add an RTL story and baseline.

verified.reason: The loop gap is real. The marqueeTrack is width:max-content in a flex layer, so in RTL the copies extend to the left while the keyframe translates to -50%, which scrolls into blank space at the right. There is no RTL rule. But the 'fades the wrong edge' part is wrong: the mask runs transparent to black to black to transparent, the same on both edges. The ticker also animates only while overflowing, on hover or focus (or autoplay), and the resting state is a correct truncated copy. This is a cosmetic RTL flaw during hover, not a blocker.

findings.subject: sidebar

findings.subject: sidebar

findings.subject: sidebar-nav-tree
